applicable_conditions: When comparing candidate_01 (delays 0s and 10s) showing early loss of both J-15s versus baseline (5s, 20s) where they survived to attack.
When execution succeeded but scoring evidence is missing.
When weapon release traces show no air-fired missiles for the affected sorties.
counter_conditions: If J-15 early losses occur even with baseline delays in some seeds, the association weakens.
If defender behavior varies drastically across seeds, delay effect may be masked.
If no loss occurs with some delay values, the pattern may be non-monotonic or random.
hypothesis: Launch_delay_seconds on air sorties may be associated with whether J-15 aircraft are lost before reaching attack range, but missing evidence prevents confirming a direct cause.

recommended_pattern.summary: Design a controlled experiment: vary only the launch_delay_seconds for both sorties across several values (e.g., 0,5,10,15,20) while keeping all other parameters constant, and use multiple random seeds per configuration. Record whether J-15s reach attack range. This will test if early delay is systematically linked to pre-attack loss, without implying a specific intercept mechanism.
